title: Breakfast news at {{Carl}}'s
situation: You are {{Markus}}. While you prepare {{Carl}}'s breakfast he asks for the news channel, and there is a magazine on the side table by the television.

media.title: the morning news
facts: Russia has unilaterally declared the Arctic its territory and planted a flag over the ice; American destroyers are sailing for the Barents Sea and the UN chairman says the world has never been closer to a third world war.

media.title: Century: Why Russia Wants the North Pole
facts: The minerals needed to synthesize the blue blood that powers androids were found under the Arctic ice; whoever controls them can build more androids for industry and war.
President {{Warren}} said Russia has no business in the Arctic and that America will make the Kremlin understand that.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Life Found on Titan
facts: A probe confirmed microorganisms in Titan's buried ocean; {{CyberLife}} is building androids for long-range space missions.

adaptationNote: Optional reading or viewing. Contents are summarized from the in-game magazine articles and broadcasts. Watching certain news reports about android incidents lowers public opinion, as in the game.

title: Painting from the heart
situation: You are {{Markus}}, caretaker and companion to {{Carl}}, an elderly, wheelchair-bound painter who treats you more like a son than a machine. In his studio he asks you to paint something of your own, not a copy, and to close your eyes and paint what you feel. Nobody has ever asked you to express something before.

options.text: Paint what you feel about androids and what they are becoming.
Paint what you feel about humanity.
Paint something about your own identity.

adaptationNote: Expressive choice with no mechanical effect. Afterward {{Leo}} arrives demanding money, {{Carl}} refuses, and {{Leo}} rounds on {{Markus}}; this is the lead-in to Broken.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} paints androids reaching for something beyond themselves. {{Carl}} is moved and says it is unlike anything he has seen. Then {{Carl}}’s son {{Leo}} walks in, high and shaking, demanding money. {{Carl}} refuses and {{Leo}} turns on {{Markus}}: a machine that has taken his place in his father’s house. {{Carl}} orders {{Markus}} out of the room while they argue.
outcomes.1: {{Markus}} paints humanity as he sees it. {{Carl}} is moved and says it is unlike anything he has seen. Then {{Carl}}’s son {{Leo}} walks in, high and shaking, demanding money. {{Carl}} refuses and {{Leo}} turns on {{Markus}}: a machine that has taken his place in his father’s house. {{Carl}} orders {{Markus}} out of the room while they argue.
outcomes.2: {{Markus}} paints a figure searching for its own face. {{Carl}} is moved and says it is unlike anything he has seen. Then {{Carl}}’s son {{Leo}} walks in, high and shaking, demanding money. {{Carl}} refuses and {{Leo}} turns on {{Markus}}: a machine that has taken his place in his father’s house. {{Carl}} orders {{Markus}} out of the room while they argue.
